content.intro: This lesson covers Cross-Platform Libraries and Portable Code. It sits in Module 26, WebAssembly and Cross-Platform Rust, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-Platform Libraries and Portable Code matters when you work with portable modules and explicit host interfaces. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: WebAssembly provides a portable execution target, but browser or host access still depends on an explicit interface. Check target-specific toolchains, data conversion, and host permissions.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Cross-Platform Libraries and Portable Code, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. WebAssembly output runs inside a host environment with an explicit interface; producing a wasm artifact does not automatically grant browser, file, or network access.

content_blocks.text: Do not assume Cross-Platform Libraries and Portable Code guarantees more than it actually does. Reduce a failure to a small reproducer, read the full compiler diagnostic or error value, consult the matching official reference, and change one assumption at a time.
